text: For a group homomorphism φ: G → H, which statement is correct?
choices: The kernel of φ is a subgroup of the codomain H
The kernel of φ is always a normal subgroup of G, and G/ker φ ≅ im φ
φ is injective if and only if ker φ = G
The image of φ is always a normal subgroup of H
explanation: Kernels are always normal in the domain G, and the first isomorphism theorem gives G/ker φ ≅ im φ. The kernel is a subgroup of G (not H), so A is wrong; φ is injective iff ker φ is trivial ({e}), not all of G, so C is wrong; the image need not be normal in H, so D is wrong.
